items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Judith sang – she sings the solo of Wendell Culley on Little Darlin’. We played in the south of France.

ctx.x: You’re remarkable. How do you go about – you’ve influenced many vocalists. I think that there’s a lineage that certainly comes through you and goes on. How do you train other vocalists? For instance, I know, in your group, you’ve had different baritones – baritone singers. How do you indoctrinate them into the Hendricks concept.

I use what I said in my short jazz poem. I wrote the shortest jazz poem. You know that jazz poem. “Listen.” I tell them that if you listen, and you hear the horn, and you sing what you hear, then I don’t have to tell you anything. You got it right. One of the students that I’ve heard actually do that is Judith. Judith sang – she sings the solo of Wendell Culley on Little Darlin’. We played in the south of France. A man of about 60 years old came backstage and says, “Incroyable, incroyable. She sings ze solo…
